episodes.171541: High pressure was established across the lower Mid-Atlantic during the evening of August 25th, allowing for only widely-scattered showers and thunderstorm development, mainly confined along and west of the Blue Ridge.  Wind speeds in the lower levels of the atmosphere were generally less than 10 mph from the northwest, supporting only very slow movement of the convection.  Dry air associated with the high pressure limited precipitable water values that evening to 1.23 inches per the August 26th 00Z upper air sounding performed by NWS Blacksburg, which is very near the 50th percentile for late August.  One slow moving thunderstorm developed over northern Roanoke County and tracked slowly southeast along the Botetourt County line.  The storm intensified near the community of Cloverdale and produced heavy rainfall between 8 pm and 10 pm EDT at rates of 2 to locally 4 inches per hour.  Some flooding issues were noted, particularly along Tinker Creek which rose 8 feet in under 2 hours.  While the rainfall was intense and justified the issuance of a flash flood warning given the higher population density of the area, the small footprint of the heavy rain, semi-rural nature of the area impacted and the late evening hour limited evidence of flash flooding in the area.
episodes.171601: Monsoon moisture increased across the Four Corners region as a shortwave disturbance lifted overhead. This led to an uptick in shower and thunderstorm activity. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain which led to localized flash flooding in portions of San Juan County.
episodes.171602: Monsoon moisture increased across the Four Corners region as a shortwave disturbance lifted overhead. This led to an uptick in shower and thunderstorm activity. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain which led to localized debris flows in portions of Mesa and Ouray counties. Additionally, moderate instability led to some stronger thunderstorms; one of which produced a funnel cloud in Dolores County.
episodes.171608: Isolated thunderstorms formed during the heat of the afternoon. There was very little in the way of large-scale forcing for storms to develop, and the storm updrafts were not particularly strong based on radar observations. One of the storms produced a microburst.
episodes.171637: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed on the afternoon of the 25th over east-central Wyoming, mainly across Converse and Niobrara Counties. These storms produced strong winds, large hail, and large accumulations of hail.
episodes.171755: A rather strong cold front approached Vermont, during the afternoon and evening hours of August 26th in a marginally unstable air mass. A few thunderstorms developed in New York and moved into western Vermont. One such storm during the evening hours produced a very small, brief but intense microburst in Clarendon that destroyed a barn and a dozen or so trees.  Five people were trapped, then rescued with minor injuries but 75 cattle (cows) were trapped with 50 needing to be euthanized.
episodes.171923: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the Brevard County coast and a waterspout offshore of Volusia County.
episodes.171933: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced localized wind damage over Albemarle County.
episodes.172256: Severe thunderstorms developed over northern Crook County and slowly tracked to the east-southeast. Hail around quarter size fell with the storms.
episodes.172258: A severe thunderstorm developed over northeastern Campbell County and tracked east into Crook County. The storm produced large hail in the Oshoto area.
episodes.172377: A cold front swept southeastward across Lake Erie during the morning through early afternoon of the 26th and encountered a warm sector marine boundary layer exhibiting moderate instability and very weak convective inhibition, which allowed the front to trigger isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms. The thermodynamic environment and low-level convergence/horizontal wind shear along the front also led to the development of a couple non-mesocyclonic waterspouts near Presque Isle State Park, PA.
episodes.172603: An inverted trough of low pressure over the area interacted with the sea breezes over a moist airmass in light flow. Aloft, broad troughing over the lower Mississippi Valley and ridging over the Bahamas continued west-southwesterly flow maintaining the anomalously moist airmass over the area, with PWATs near 2.2 inches. Scattered to numerous showers and storms developed along the Atlantic sea breeze as it slowly shifted inland in the afternoon. Storms backbuilded and remained stationary over portions of Flagler county causing street flooding. The Gulf and Atlantic sea breezes merged along the I-75 corridor in the evening causing heavy downpours and street flooding in Columbia county. About 3 to 4 inches of rain fell within 90 minutes. Slow-moving storms also brought 3.50 inches to the Okefenokee swamp.
episodes.172606: An inverted trough over the waters helped ignite low-topped convection which then produced a waterspout off of Atlantic beach around 12:40 PM.
episodes.172889: A cold front moved into a warm and humid air mass, triggered scattered severe thunderstorms in southern New England during the mid and late afternoon.
episodes.172890: A cold front moved into a warm and humid air mass, triggered scattered severe thunderstorms in southern New England during the mid and late afternoon.
episodes.172891: A cold front moved into a warm and humid air mass, triggered scattered severe thunderstorms in southern New England during the mid and late afternoon.
episodes.173104: A persistent upper low over Washington favored ample moisture transport into the area. Shear was fairly limited throughout, hence wind gusts were the main concern with these storms, along with potential for heavy rain. Small hail was expected, but a few reports of severe level hail were relayed.
episodes.173225: A low pressure system spinning over northern Louisiana and southern Arkansas brought several rounds of showers and thunderstorms producing heavy rain to Mississippi August 24th through 25th. This resulted in widespread flooding of roads, homes, and businesses around the state.
episodes.173382: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across the region as a frontal system pushed through. A few of these storms became severe downing trees and power lines. A localized area of widespread straight-line wind damage occurred near Earlton in Greene County downing trees and wires as well as damaging structures.
episodes.173383: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across the region as a frontal system pushed through. A few of these storms became severe downing trees and power lines.
episodes.173450: Severe thunderstorms fired up along a pre-frontal trough ahead of a cold front. The storms moved over the waters and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.173452: Severe thunderstorms fired up along a pre-frontal trough ahead of a cold front. The storms moved over southern CT and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.173460: An inverted trough of low pressure over the area interacted with the sea breezes over a moist airmass in light flow. Aloft, broad troughing over the lower Mississippi Valley and ridging over the Bahamas continued west-southwesterly flow maintaining the anomalously moist airmass over the area, with PWATs near 2.2 inches. Scattered to numerous showers and storms developed along the Atlantic sea breeze as it slowly shifted inland in the afternoon. Storms backbuilded and remained stationary over portions of Flagler county causing street flooding. The Gulf and Atlantic sea breezes merged along the I-75 corridor in the evening causing heavy downpours and street flooding in Columbia county. About 3 to 4 inches of rain fell within 90 minutes. Slow-moving storms also brought 3.50 inches to the Okefenokee swamp.
episodes.173538: A cold front moved into the region and stalled while a weakness aloft lingered over area. This provided multiple days of rain while soils were already saturated from previous events. Flash flooded resulted from the prolonged rain.
episodes.173669: Isolated thunderstorms developed across the North Carolina mountains during the evening. One storm produced brief damaging wind gusts on Eastern Band of Cherokee Indian land.
episodes.173712: A closed Low over the region shifted over North Idaho and increased instability over the area. The instability mixed with afternoon convection to develop isolated thunderstorms.
episodes.173806: Monsoon moisture fueled scattered thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. A few storms produced flash flooding and severe weather.
episodes.173807: Monsoon moisture fueled scattered thunderstorms over southeast California. Many storms produced flash flooding, and a few produced severe weather.
episodes.173808: Monsoon moisture fueled scattered thunderstorms over southern Nevada. A few storms produced flash flooding and severe weather.
episodes.173841: Numerous showers and thunderstorms affected southern and eastern Middle Tennessee during the afternoon of August 26. One storm produced wind damage and flooding in Lawrence County.
episodes.173887: A cold front moved through the region. A few strong to severe storms developed with reports of damaging winds.
episodes.173944: Regenerating morning convection anchored over eastern portions of Hamblen County and Morristown produced flash flooding.
episodes.173949: Isolated thunderstorms moved erratically across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. In the Tucson Metro, localized flash flooding occurred and a landspout was spotted.
episodes.174023: Enough monsoon moisture remained over northern Arizona for scattered thunderstorms with isolated marginally severe storms.
episodes.174035: A pre-frontal trough ahead of strong cold front and surface low over New York state interacted with a hot and humid airmass on the afternoon of August 26th.  A line of thunderstorms developed across Vermont and quickly moved across the state from west to east during the early to mid afternoon hours.  Some storms embedded within the line become severe bringing damaging wind gusts and large hail.  Severe weather was more concentrated along the Connecticut River Valley and Lakes Region.
episodes.174036: A pre-frontal trough ahead of strong cold front and surface low over New York state interacted with a hot and humid airmass on the afternoon of August 26th. A line of thunderstorms developed across Vermont and quickly moved across New Hampshire from west to east during the early to mid afternoon hours. The line of storms reached York and Oxford County by mid-afternoon.  The storms were weakening before a storm re-strengthened over Portland and the Marine waters causing significant damage on Peaks Island waterfront area.
episodes.174037: A pre-frontal trough ahead of strong cold front and surface low over New York state interacted with a hot and humid airmass on the afternoon of August 26th. A line of thunderstorms developed across Vermont and quickly moved across New Hampshire from west to east during the early to mid afternoon hours. The line of storms reached York and Oxford County by mid-afternoon. The line of storms held together as it crossed the Seacoast and Southern Maine waters were very strong wind gusts were reported.
